processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental steel was melted and cast in a 50 kg vacuum induction furnace and then air cooled to RT.
The ingot was reheated to 1250 °C and held for 2 h for homogenization.
Ingot forged into round bars with a diameter of 60 mm followed by cooling to RT in the furnace; starting and finishing forging temperatures were 1100 and 950 °C.

processing_steps.method: uniaxial tensile test (tensile deformation to fracture)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Tensile deformed to fracture at -77 °C on a YYF-50 tensile tester; dry ice-alcohol mixture used as cooling medium; strain rate 0.001 s^-1 (slow enough to avoid frictional heat); extensometer used; three tensile samples with parallel length 32 mm, width 5 mm and thickness 1.5 mm tested per condition and averaged.

structures.overall_structure: Tensile-deformed (uniform deformation section) austenite deformed by planar glide; uniform and dense microbands along {111} planes, no mechanical twins (unlike the -196 °C sample). Crystal orientation of deformed austenite grains concentrates in {111} and {001}.

microstructure_list.region: uniform deformation section, ~10 mm from the fracture (region not affected by necking)

defects.type: geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) accumulating at LAGBs
defects.lattice_distortion: GND/kernel average misorientation maps 0-3°; high misorientation concentrated along intra-granular bands and slip/microband traces

grain_structure.texture: crystal orientation concentrated in {111} and {001}; LAGBs (2–15°) 63.0%, HAGBs (>15°) 37.0%

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: GNDs accumulate at LAGBs, indicating a more severe local deformation of these regions in the -77 °C tensile sample.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar glide of dislocations; deformation proceeds by planar glide producing uniform and dense microbands oriented along {111} planes; no mechanical twinning (unlike -196 °C).
interfaces.phase_evolution: No deformation-induced martensitic transformation and no mechanical twinning; deformation accommodated solely by planar glide/microband formation.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: parallel length 32 mm, width 5 mm, thickness 1.5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: YYF-50 tensile tester, deformation to fracture, carried out in the cooling medium; extensometer used; 3 samples per condition averaged

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve (Fig. 2a) and true stress-strain plus work hardening rate curves (Fig. 2b) at -77 °C; near-linear work hardening rate with strain (contrasting with RT where it continuously decreases).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Both tensile strength and elongation increase as the deformation temperature decreases (negative temperature dependence of strength); lower SFE at lower temperature promotes dislocation planar glide, raising the work hardening rate, LAGB fraction and uniform deformation.

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) - IPF, grain boundary (GB) and GND (kernel average misorientation) maps
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac scanning electron microscope (SEM)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: step size 0.5 μm; performed on the polished uniformly deformed section ~10 mm from the fracture
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze the tensile deformed microstructure (crystal orientation, LAGB/HAGB fractions, GND distribution)
characterization_methods.key_findings: -77 °C tensile sample: no mechanical twins; LAGB (2–15°) 63.0% and HAGB (>15°) 37.0%; crystal orientation concentrated in {111} and {001}; GNDs accumulate at LAGBs.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM, bright-field) with selected area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tecnai F30 field emission TEM; specimens double-jet thinned with a Struers TenuPol-5 Twin-Jet Electropolisher (6% perchloric acid + 94% glacial acetic acid)
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe deformation features (microbands, dislocations) of the tensile-deformed samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the -77 °C sample: microbands with traces of {111} slip planes and a dislocation-dense matrix; no mechanical twins (mechanical twins observed only at -196 °C).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Test temperature -77 °C (dry ice-alcohol), strain rate 0.001 s^-1, 3 samples per condition
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure tensile stress-strain response and mechanical properties (YS, UTS, elongation) and fracture behavior
characterization_methods.key_findings: At -77 °C both strength and elongation are higher than at RT; work hardening rate increases as deformation temperature decreases (negative temperature dependence of strength).

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical thermodynamic estimation of stacking fault energy (SFE)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Thermodynamic parameter expressions from Ref. [6] (Table 1); SFE equation after Ref. [31]

analytical_models.equation_role: SFE = 2ρ_A ΔG^{γ→ε} + 2σ^{γ/ε} (equation 2); ρ_A from equation (3), ΔG^{γ→ε} from equation (4)
analytical_models.model_note: SFE of the experimental Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si steel estimated to be 32, 40 and 61 mJ/m^2 at -196 °C, -77 °C and RT respectively; the -77 °C value is 40 mJ/m^2. This SFE is high enough to suppress DIMT but allows planar glide.

computational_details.simulation_method: Work-hardening analysis using the Hollomon equation (two-stage fit)

analytical_models.equation_role: σ = K ε^n ; lnσ = lnK + n lnε (equations 5-6); slope n of lnσ-lnε gives work hardening exponent
analytical_models.model_note: Two-stage work hardening behavior; n1 is the slope in the low-strain (early uniform plastic deformation) region and n2 the slope in the high-strain region. Both stage slopes increase as the tensile temperature decreases.

unmapped_findings: The -77 °C tensile-deformed sample shows no mechanical twins; deformation proceeds by planar glide producing uniform and dense microbands, and SAED indicates these bands are oriented along {111} planes.

Grain boundary fractions of the -77 °C tensile-deformed sample: LAGB (2–15°) = 63.0%, HAGB (>15°) = 37.0% (Fig. 3e); the LAGB fraction increases as the deformation temperature decreases (70.2% at -196 °C, 63.0% at -77 °C, 56.0% at RT).
The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the experimental steel at -77 °C is estimated to be 40 mJ/m^2 (32 mJ/m^2 at -196 °C and 61 mJ/m^2 at RT).
Crystal orientation of the deformed austenite grains concentrates in {111} and {001} as a result of coordinated plastic deformation.

The work hardening rate of the -77 °C sample shows a near-linear variation with strain, whereas at RT a continuous decrease is observed; the work hardening rate increases as deformation temperature decreases.
Estimated density by the Kim et al. equation is 7.078 g/cm^3, while the measured density is 7.114 g/cm^3 (alloy-level property of the same experimental steel).
